title: "Glossary"
---

```{r}
#| label: stats
#| include: false
s <- jsonlite::read_json("data/site_stats.json")
```

The words this site uses, in the sense it uses them. Where a word means one
thing to an ecologist and another on Redivis, the entry says which is meant.
The [standard](standard.html) is the full statement of the format; this page
is a reminder.

## Counting the corpus

The corpus now holds `r s$n_tables` tables from `r s$n_deposits` deposits.

### Deposit {#deposit}

The source the data came from: one published dataset with its own DOI or
archive record, on Dryad, Zenodo, figshare, ScienceBase, a data portal, or
the example data of an R package. eco never calls a deposit a "dataset",
because on Redivis that word means something else (see [shard](#shard)).
`eco_list_deposits()` in the [R package](r.html) lists them, with the
tables built from each.

### Table {#table}

One eco table: the observations from one survey design with one kind of
response, from one deposit. A deposit with, say, an occupancy survey and a
mark-recapture study yields two tables; a deposit with one survey yields
one. A table is a [core](#core) plus its [side tables](#side-tables), and is
named `author_year_taxonOrPlace_type` (for example
`kery_2008_willowtit_occ`). `eco_list_tables()` lists them.

### Core {#core}

The table's main file, one row per survey of one unit for one taxon, with
the columns `unit`, `taxon` and `y` and any of the others below. "Core
table" means the same thing.

### Side tables {#side-tables}

Small files that travel with a core and share its name plus a suffix:
`__taxa` (each taxon code with its scientific name and GBIF key, always
present), `__periods` (dates and facts about each primary period),
`__units` (the sampling frame, including units never surveyed), `__traps`
(trap locations, for spatial capture-recapture) and `__survey_taxa` (which
taxa were looked for at which surveys, where that varied). In the metadata
file they are listed under `sideTables`.

## Redivis

The tables are published on [Redivis](https://redivis.com/datasets/4j5q),
which has its own words for things.

### Shard {#shard}

One of the Redivis datasets that hold the cores and side tables:
`datapages.eco`, `datapages.eco_2`, and so on. Redivis caps a dataset at 1000
entries, so a new shard is started when the last one fills. Each table, with
its side tables, is in exactly one shard; the R package finds it for you.
The metadata about all tables is in a separate Redivis dataset, `eco_meta`.

### Entry {#entry}

One physical table on Redivis. A table with a `__taxa` and a `__periods`
side table is three entries; a very large core uploaded in parts is one
entry per part. Entries matter only for uploading and for Redivis' cap; when
the site counts the corpus it counts tables.

## Inside a table

### Unit {#unit}

The thing with the latent state the model estimates: a site, a camera
station, a pond, a transect, or, in capture-recapture, an individual animal.

### Taxon {#taxon}

A short, stable species code (or a code for a genus or species group, where
that is what the source recorded), resolved to a scientific name in
`__taxa`. Every table has the column, even with one species.

### y {#y}

The observation: a 0/1 detection, a count, or a coded state, as declared by
the table's [response type](#responsetype). It is never missing.

### Period {#period}

A primary period: a season, year or session, numbered in time order. The
state (occupied, alive, abundance) may change between periods.

### Occasion {#occasion}

A repeat survey within a period: a visit, a camera-day, a trap night, a
sample. Whether the state is assumed constant across occasions is stated in
the table's metadata (`closure`).

### Survey set {#survey-set}

Which unit, period and occasion combinations were actually surveyed. In eco
a row exists only where a survey happened, so a 0 means "surveyed, not
detected" and a missing row means "not surveyed". Each table says what its
survey set rests on (`surveyEvidence`): a deposited list of surveys, an
effort table, a matrix that tells blanks from zeros, the source's own rows,
or, flagged as `inferred`, a rule the script states.

### Response type {#responsetype}

What `y` means, declared as `responseType` in the table's metadata:
`detection` (0/1), `count`, `state` (a coded latent state, such as breeding
or not), `ordinal` (an ordered index, such as a calling index),
`binomial_count` (occasions with a detection out of `obs_trials`),
`multinomial_cell` (removal, double-observer or distance-bin counts) or
`detection_event` (one row per detection). See
[the standard, E2](standard.html).
